newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela to slash red tape, boost gold production.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela to slash red tape, boost gold production.

text.p: Venezuelan legal gold production could rise to 92 tonnes per year in the next two years from the current level of 12 tonnes as part of a new mining initiative that will slash red tape, a government official said.
"Last year, Venezuela produced 12 tonnes legally and an estimated 35 tonnes were produced by illegal miners," Americo Martin, the Planning Ministry's mining adviser, told reporters.

But following a new inter-ministerial initiative that will slash red tape and the multiple and overlapping mining permissions currently required from various ministries, "gold production could rise to 50 tonnes per year and thence 92 tonnes," said Martin.
Martin said the government would be piloting the new streamlined approach to granting gold mining concessions in western Bolivar state's Imataca forest reserve.
"El Dorado still exists, and it's in Imataca," he said.

Mining companies have long complained that overly-complex regulations, and poor coordination between ministries, had slowed development of the sector "which could be the most advanced in Latin America," Martin added.
"Venezuela's mining opening is almost as import as its oil opening. Venezuela is a sleeping lion that will wake up," Martin said.
Martin added that the long-awaited new mining law would also soon be passed be Congress. "There are only a few small points to clear-up. We'll see it soon."
He could not shed any light, however, on the on-going dispute between gold giant Placer Dome and Canadian minor Crystallex over property rights to the gold rich Las Cristinas concession.
"We'll have to wait on the Supreme Court's decision," he said.
